excerpts.text: At dusk the courier reached the wind-scoured pass below a rusted watchtower, carrying a rain-dark satchel sealed with ash. No one answered the signal bell, but boot prints ringed the threshold and vanished into the shale. When the courier touched the gate, a hidden mechanism groaned awake beneath the stone. The Cartographer entered the prose as pressure around the latch, not yet as a body. A thumb-wide crescent of dark wax had been pressed into the metal, too deliberate to be weather and too quiet to be warning. "That mark makes the scene suspect the Xerofag," came the storyteller's low restraint, and the Wax Clerk became a name the room had almost hidden.
